identification: Aria parlour-size steel-string acoustic, 12-fret neck join (body meets neck at the 12th fret), slotted headstock with open-gear three-a-side tuners, solid-looking cedar or red spruce top, abalone top purfling and abalone ring rosette, rosewood-type binding and fingerboard with dot inlays, rectangular rosewood bridge with white pins, dark reddish (rosewood-look) sides. In an SKB-style moulded hard case with green plush lining. A Martin 00-42/'Historic' parlour styling, well above Aria's entry parlours. Model code on the soundhole label is partly legible: 'AP-?TS-N' or 'AP-STD-N' style, serial about 111x40xx88; I could not resolve it. Aria's own AP-STD (solid cedar, maple binding, slotted, 12-fret) and AP-DLX (solid spruce, 12-fret) are the nearest catalogue matches, but neither lists abalone, so this may be a deluxe/limited Aria parlour or an older Japanese model.

viewing_check: Photograph the soundhole label in good light (model code, serial, 'Made in ...'), the headstock face and back; check whether the top is solid (look at the soundhole edge for one grain layer); top cracks near the soundhole and bridge, bridge lift, neck relief, fret wear; case latches and brand (SKB?).
